claim: You can edit a stored knowledge item — reclassify it (change its destination/rights), archive it, reprocess it, or delete it — and the change PERSISTS to the durable store and is reflected on reload. An invalid action or an unknown item id is REFUSED honestly (no silent no-op, no fabricated success).
owner: anima/server.py (POST /library/edit -> _serve_library_edit, validating against intake_queue._VALID_EDIT_ACTIONS and catching KeyError), anima/intake_queue.py (edit_item -> reroute_item/set_state/delete_item; the append-only audit trail), anima/web/index.html (the per-row .lactions Reprocess/Archive/Delete buttons -> apiFetch('/library/edit') -> loadLibrary refresh)

killer_test.name: edit_persists_on_reload_and_unknown_id_or_action_is_refused
killer_test.setup: Hermetic temp store. Seed one reference (intake_queue.add_reference). (A) RECLASSIFY: edit_item(action='reroute', new_destination, new_rights) returns (item, audit) whose audit.from!=audit.to; a FRESH intake_queue.references() read from disk shows the new destination+rights persisted. (B) The change is reflected through the SAME server handler the UI calls: server._serve_library_edit(action='archive') returns ok=True and the queue record is now 'archived' on a fresh get_record(). (C) HONEST REFUSAL: _serve_library_edit on an unknown id returns ok=False with an error (KeyError surfaced, not crashed); an unknown action returns ok=False (must be one of the valid actions); a missing id returns ok=False. Nothing is fabricated and nothing else mutates. Real .anima byte-unchanged. scripts/certify_memory_editor.py is the executable form.
killer_test.prompt: reclassify this note as an authoritative source

known_gaps: The web UI surfaces Reprocess/Archive/Delete as one-tap buttons; 'reroute' (reclassify destination/rights) is exercised through the same /library/edit endpoint + edit_item backend (the UI exposes it via the section model rather than a dedicated button). The endpoint + persistence are proven for all four actions.
Editing is deterministic (no model); the cert proves persistence + honest refusal, not any model-written narration of the change.
